newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: 25 non-Africans on board of hijacked plane-sources.
newsitem.headline: 25 non-Africans on board of hijacked plane-sources.

text.p: Ethiopian Airlines will issue on Sunday a passenger list from the hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane that crashed near the Comoro Islands on Saturday but aviation sources said at least 25 non-Africans were on board.

The aviation sources in Nairobi said seven Britons, four French, three Italians, two Americans, eight Israelis and Hungary's ambassador to Ethiopia and Kenya were among the passengers on the hijacked plane.
There was no information about whether or not the Hungarian ambassador had survived.
The Italian news agency ANSA reported that three Italians were among the survivors, including two employees at the Italian embassy in Addis Ababa.

Ethiopia's Immigration Department, which holds the passenger manifest and boarding pass list, was not available on Saturday evening, Abebe Damassa, spokesman for the airline, told Reuters. The airline will issue the list on Sunday, he added.
Sources close to the airline said 47 of the 163 passengers and 12 crew aboard the plane were foreigners from some 21 countries, most of them from Europe.

Ethiopia's President in a message on state television expressed shock and offered condolences to the families of the passengers and crew who died when the plane crashed into the sea after apparently running out of fuel.
He said the accident was "the result of criminal activities by terrorists whose identy and nationality has not yet been established".
So far 50 survivors have been found and 50 people have been confirmed dead in the crash.
